target.name: Ephos
target.founder: Andrea Rocchetto, Francesco Ceccarelli, Ciro Pentangelo

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $42M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Chips & Semiconductors. Range: $2.0B - $11.0B.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 20.5x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Ephos is a seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised €41.5M in EU funding plus $8.5M in seed capital. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 private peers (including SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, and d-Matrix) and 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $42M raised proxy, implying a $104M valuation. Peer-median anchoring across three same-sector, same-stage private comparables yields a $2.3B median valuation, with a range of $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp P/S anchoring is not applicable: while the semiconductor sector median trades at 20.5x revenue across the three public tickers, Ephos's revenue remains undisclosed, precluding this method.

The two applicable methods generate a wide implied range: $88M (conservative), $1.2B (median), and $2.7B (high). This spread reflects the tension between stage-based mechanics (suggesting ~$104M) and peer-comparable valuations anchored to Series A stage comparables. Key uncertainties include Ephos's actual revenue run-rate, capital efficiency relative to peers, and the specific technology differentiation that would justify positioning within the $2.0B–$11.0B peer range versus the lower stage-progression anchor.
